system_name: APIDS (Automated Prohibited Item Detection) Algorithms Deployment
department: Canadian Air Transport Security Authority / L’Administration canadienne de sûreté du transport aérien
description: Assessment and trial of different APIDS algorithms on multi-view and CT x-rays used at PBS. OEMs and third party companies are developing object recognition algorithms to work in conjunction with explosive detection algorithms to detect potential threats. Materials absorb x-rays at different rates based on their density and atomic number, creating a contrast image of luggage contents.  Explosive detection algorithm analyzes the densities/atomic number and size of items in a bag  and compares the results against a known list of explosives and threat masses prescribed by the regulators to identify items of concern. Algorithms are developed by the equipment suppliers and are updated every several years based on new regulation. Each algorithm is rigorously tested by TSA and ECAC regulators before certification using real explosives. CATSA works with Transport Canada to assess whether new algorithms need to be rolled out to CATSA’s fleet of equipment.

Les équipementiers et les entreprises tierces développent des algorithmes de reconnaissance d'objets qui fonctionnent en conjonction avec des algorithmes de détection d'explosifs pour détecter les menaces potentielles. Les matériaux absorbent les rayons X à des vitesses différentes en fonction de leur densité et de leur numéro atomique, créant ainsi une image contrastée du contenu des bagages. department: Canadian Space Agency / Agence spatiale canadienne
description: PAT is intended to support operators’ space robotics training by creating a state-of-the-art learning experience that includes both theoretical knowledge and practical application. Familiarization with the Mobile Servicing System (MSS, aka Canadarm2) and its robotics work station (RWS) operational environment is the first lesson new recruits receive when taking the robotics training at CSA. Under this initiative, PAT will provide this familiarization training, first for the MSS currently on the International Space Station, and eventually for the Gateway External Robotics System (Canadarm3) located on the new Gateway Station orbiting the Moon. The goal is to provide a comprehensive learning experience for CSA personnel, ensuring they are well equipped to handle current and future space missions. This project aims to set a new benchmark for adaptive learning within the CSA by integrating AI to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness.
purpose: PAT will significantly increase the effectiveness of the training programs by reducing the costs for one-on-one instruction, trainee travel, and trainee and instructor logistics. This has the potential to reduce costs significantly for CSA’s modern space missions and operations involving the Canadarm technology. PAT can be extended to other lessons and other training applications and can be used to complement existing training delivery methods.

system_name: Remote Observation of Watercraft on Roads
department: Fisheries and Oceans Canada / Pêches et Océans Canada
description:
The Aquatic Invasive Species Program is proposing to launch a pilot initiative aimed at addressing a critical knowledge gap in our understanding the spread of aquatic invasive species.  Invasive species can attach to boats, trailers, and related equipment—a process commonly referred to as the "stowaway pathway"—which enables their unintentional spread across ecosystems when watercraft are transported between water bodies. The AIS Program is seeking to understand watercraft movement into Canada via international land border crossings. Currently, the extent of this "stowaway" pathway remains largely unquantified.
To address this, the pilot will deploy remote camera systems at select border entry points to capture imagery of incoming vehicles. Leveraging machine learning, the system will automatically identify and flag images containing watercraft.

description: The Meteorological Services of Canada (MSC) and Science & Technology Branch of ECCC are actively exploring AI for weather prediction. This roadmap will drive forward key initiatives, such as the exploration of energy-efficient AI weather models (e.g. GraphCast, ForeCastNet and AIFS) and the development of an all-Canadian model called PARADIS (Physically-inspired Advection, Reaction and Diffusion on the Sphere) a hybrid weather prediction system called "spectral nudging" that combines traditional forecasting methods with AI.
purpose: This explorating, development and future production will increase ECCC's ability to support earlier detection of weather events and their impacts; improve the timeliness and accuracy of forecasts; improve flood forecasting; and, improve models to more accurately represent how nature really works.

description: To understand what portion of Canada’s development programming in agriculture and food aligns with the Ceres2030 10 high-impact interventions to meet the United Nation Sustainable Development Goal 2 towards “zero hunger.” The aim of this work is to use machine learning to extract certain project characteristics, features and details at the output and activity level to enhance the details currently found in existing departmental reporting. This will help to elaborate causal relationships of outputs and activities that are buried within project documents and project outcomes presented in reports. This process will lead to building a platform for portfolio analysis and future predictive analysis.  This approach will inform the extent to which interventions and approaches, either individually and jointly, are in alignment with the Ceres2030 Interventions and meeting strategic, programmatic and policy needs and beyond.

These are algorithmically mapped to high-impact strategies from the Ceres2030 framework. The data is integrated into dashboards for visualization and decision support. system_name: Enhanced Reporting Capabilities for International Assistance Grants and Contributions
department: Global Affairs Canada / Affaires mondiales Canada
description: Global Affairs Canada is responsible for managing most of Canada's international assistance funding, and its staff are often required to assess alignment between project funding and policy objectives. Assessing projects against evolving and emerging policy markers is time consuming, and GAC looked for risk-informed methods to automate these assessments. Using manual assessments as a gold standard, GAC tested approaches to understand the trade-off between accuracy, transparency, and cost. It implementd methods using generative AI to encode the assessment frameworks and the domain knowledge of experienced evaluators. This approach assigns policy markers based on project summaries generated during GAC’s existing processes. Multiple policy markers have been implemented within a web-based tool which is currently in validation. The tool has an accuracy comparable to expert assessors and produces an accompanying explanation to allow expert oversight.

description: Situational Awareness is a custom application built by the National Research Council, which allows Global Affairs Canada to proactively monitor information originating from traditional news and social media sources.  The platform uses Support Vector Machine libraries to score the news articles as they are ingested.
purpose: The platform utilizes scheduled data ingestion via Factiva and Twitter APIs, retrieving news and tweets at 15-minute intervals. Textual analysis employs machine translation, geo-tagging, named entity recognition, quotation attribution, and VAD sentiment scoring. Relevance is computed using a support vector machine, while VAD quantifies valence, arousal, and dominance for quoted statements. Results are visualized as ranked lists, interactive maps, and stance matrices for advanced insight.

description: This project automates the processing of applications for some Temporary Resident Visas and Work Permits made under the Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel initiative (CUAET). Automation will also be applied to administrative steps that do not require human intervention. system_name: Enhance Transportation Infrastructure Resiliency through Bridge Monitoring
department: National Research Council Canada / Conseil national de recherches Canada
description: Canada has more than 50,000 publicly owned bridges. Many are reaching the end of their lifespan and 11% are reported to be in poor or very poor condition. While the design life of a bridge is generally 50 to 75 years, they can safely last longer with good monitoring and timely maintenance, which requires a significant public investment. The National Research Council of Canada's AI for Logistics program is addressing these challenges together with experts from Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada, Esri Canada and the University of Manitoba. They are developing improved methods for life-long monitoring of infrastructure conditions and decision support for maintenance investment by studying a highway bridge in Manitoba.  This will enhance the potential for remote bridge monitoring and reduce physical and economic risks related to bridge failure.
purpose: When completed, the project will provide an AI-based bridge health predictor that governments could use to support decision-makers in their operation and investment in bridge maintenance, renewal or replacement.

description: As their numbers surge, uncrewed aerial systems (UASs), commonly known as drones, will pose more hazards than ever to privacy, security, lives, homes and infrastructure. Over the past 4 years, an R&D team of engineers and scientists from the NRC's Digital Technologies Research Centre and the DRDC have developed an innovative technological solution for passively spotting drones in cluttered settings. department: National Research Council Canada / Conseil national de recherches Canada
description: The system forecasts harbour ice up in the north.  Accurate and timely forecasts of sea ice conditions are crucial for safe shipping operations in the Canadian Arctic and other ice-infested waters. Sea-ice forecasts can be obtained through an optimal combination of sea-ice model output and observational data, in a manner similar to weather forecasting. However, these forecasting systems typically rely on accurate weather forecasting data to drive the sea-ice model, which is not available at high spatial resolution during the advance tactical planning stage. For this reason, seasonal sea ice forecasts are often obtained through statistical means. This Project builds on a prototype system that used artificial intelligence (AI) methods to provide state-of-the-art seasonal forecasts of sea ice conditions in the Canadian Arctic. Codeveloped with University of Waterloo.
purpose: SIFNET forecast products are now produced on a daily basis and integrated into the existing NRC-OCRE tool CASRAS (Canadian Arctic Shipping Risk Assessment System). CASRAS updates also made available to external stakeholders as of 2023.

description: Articles in scientific publications often contain hints about important emerging technologies, but signals that indicate the next big risk to national and international security are often subtle. The challenge is to detect these weak signals and assess their possible impacts on future security, then use that intelligence to reinforce defence. For the past decade, the NRC and DRDC have used scientometrics, the science of measuring and analyzing scholarly literature, to track, measure and identify technology trends in different scientific fields. The NRC, DRDC and international allies and partners have prototyped an ingenious AI solution that simplifies and improves both weak-signal detection and monitoring of emerging technologies. It also introduces new techniques for predicting the impacts of these technologies and detecting opportunities for innovation.

system_name: Canadian Geospatial Data Infrastructure Geospatial Services Web Harvester
department: Natural Resources Canada / Ressources naturelles Canada
description: Uses ML/AI to automatically identify standards-based geospatial web services (such as Web Map Service (WMS), Web Feature Service (WFS), Web Map Tile Service (WMTS) and Esri Representational State Transfer (REST) services) that provide access to geospatial data. The ML/AI identifies and filters services available for the Arctic and Canadian domain (.ca domain). Purpose of application is to help identify services that are part of the Canadian Geospatial Data Infrastructure (CGDI) and to understand how widely standards-based geospatial web services are being implemented. department: Public Safety Canada / Sécurité publique Canada
description: Agent-driven software development platform that orchestrates teams of specialized AI agents to manage the complete software development lifecycle (SDLC). Rather than individual developers using AI assistants, PSForge coordinates governed agent teams — Business Analyst, Developer, QA, DevOps, and Project Manager agents — to handle requirements analysis, code implementation, testing, deployment, and project tracking. The platform ingests requirements from GitHub Issues, decomposes them into specifications and tasks, generates tested code delivered as Pull Requests, and manages CI/CD pipelines — all with mandatory human approval gates at specification review, code review, and deployment authorization. An internal orchestration engine (OpenClaw) provides task routing, shared context management, escalation detection, configurable guardrails (file permissions, branch protection, deployment restrictions), and a full audit trail. A real-time dashboard provides visibility into team velocity, quality metrics, resource utilization, and escalated blockers.
purpose: Targets 60% cycle time reduction from issue creation to merged Pull Request versus traditional development. Enables elastic scaling of development capacity (10–50x parallel agent instances) without hiring delays or onboarding cycles. Enforces 90%+ automated test coverage on all agent-generated code. Targets 80% first-pass human approval rate on Pull Requests without revision. Maintains full human governance — agents escalate decisions exceeding their authority threshold or confidence level. Provides complete audit trail of all agent actions, decisions, API calls, and data access

description: Copilot (and its premium offering M365 Copilot) is a general-purpose generative AI solution offered to GC departments. Mid-2025 usage of Copilot is focused on personal productivity -- text generation, text editing, image generation, text summarization and translation.)  Over the next year, the PSC hopes to focus on a more enterprise-level use of Copilot through complex shared prompts and Copilot agents providing specialized chatbot capabilities from a selected corpus of documentation.
